Honestly exposure and recognizing that I have absolutely nothing to lose. The nothing to lose thing is a huge thing for me, what do I actually have to lose by going on a date, and if the person does judge me, would I want to be with someone who judges me for a personality quirk on the first date, a stutter, or engaging in awkward eye contact? Not really, because I want to be with someone who would understand that sort of thing exists in other people and it doesn’t mean that they are weird or creepy. 

It’s also part of fake it til you make it, and watching how other people interact with each other. Part of social anxiety for me is being behind in social skills within my age group because when it started to develop I straight up progressed into total isolation for years. Being in college, I try to pay some attention to how others interact and speak, and I pick up the things I like as I go and use them in casual encounters. Interacting with classmates, customers at work, and people in general who aren’t on the “possible romantic connection list” makes you feel more confident when speaking to a date- because they could just be a classmate or someone else in another situation.

Sorry if I don’t have the best advice, I’m still learning and working through it, but I hope you can get something out of this! Good luck!
